attacksAttemptedAndFailed.result: REFUTED - and this is the inverse of D-106, decided correctly
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.detail: I read both advisories in full rather than reasoning from the shared id pattern. Claude's ADV-V6-01 is titled 'parsedCellsDerivedFrom rests its durability guarantee on membership in the v4 roster, and a per-generation closed roster confers no forward protection' - a durability defect about roster scope, located at /parsedCellsDerivedFrom. Codex's CODEX-V6-A1 is titled 'The D-104 COORD snapshot was accurate when v6 froze but is no longer literally live after additive D-105' - a staleness defect about an environmental pin, located at /environmentStanding. Different field, different defect class, different remedy: one wants a forward-durable guarantee, the other wants an at-authoring label or a remeasure. They are not the same finding and must not be collapsed. The draft's characterization is exact on both counts - it names Claude's as v4-roster durability and Codex's as the D-104 COORD snapshot no longer live - and it keeps them travelling separately. This is the mirror image of D-106, where the two /date advisories genuinely were one defect and collapsing them was correct; the coordinator adjudicated each collision on content rather than applying the prior cycle's answer by reflex.
